study_notes.topic: Alphanumeric Series and Alphabet Test (Verbal Reasoning)

sections.title: Level 2 Series Strategy
sections.content: In Level 2, the series is longer and more mixed. Step 1: Carefully read the entire series. Step 2: Identify letters, numbers, and symbols separately. Step 3: Understand the given condition or rule. Step 4: Determine the required positions or counts of elements.

sections.title: Continuous Mixed Series
sections.content: In a continuous mixed series, letters, numbers, and symbols appear together. Step 1: Identify the type of each element (letter, number, symbol). Step 2: Write them in sequence. Step 3: Focus only on the elements required by the question. Step 4: Determine the answer based on pattern or position. Example: M % 8 * K $ 2 T # 9 Q @ W 4 &.

sections.title: Conditional Counting
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the condition given in the question. Step 2: Find the elements in the series that satisfy the condition. Step 3: Check the elements before and after them. Step 4: Count only the valid cases. Example: If a consonant has a symbol before it and a number after it, count only those cases.

sections.title: Element Elimination
sections.content: Step 1: Write the series clearly. Step 2: Remove certain elements according to the question (for example, all symbols and even numbers). Step 3: Form a new series. Step 4: Find the required position in the new series. Example: Identify the 12th element from the left and then count the 5th element to its right.

sections.title: Number Operations in Series
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the numbers in the series. Step 2: Check whether there is a pattern such as addition, subtraction, or multiplication. Step 3: Apply the mathematical rule. Step 4: Determine the next or related value. Example: 3, 6, 12, 24 → each step follows ×2.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Misidentifying the type of elements. 2. Counting without fully understanding the condition. 3. Not forming the new series correctly after elimination. 4. Misinterpreting the mathematical pattern.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 2, identifying the correct elements in long mixed series is important. In conditional counting, count only the elements that satisfy the condition. In element elimination, create a new series before finding positions. For number patterns, apply simple mathematical rules.

tricks.title: Element Classification Trick
tricks.explanation: First identify letters, numbers, and symbols separately in the series.
tricks.example: A 4 % B 7 → A,B letters | 4,7 numbers | % symbol.

tricks.title: Condition Highlight Method
tricks.explanation: Mark elements that satisfy the given condition before counting.
tricks.example: If a letter must have a symbol before it, check only those cases.

tricks.title: Elimination Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Remove unwanted elements first and form a new series.
tricks.example: A 2 % B 4 → removing even numbers and symbols gives A B.

tricks.title: Position Counting Rule
tricks.explanation: Always start counting positions from the new series.
tricks.example: The 12th element may change after elimination.

tricks.title: Symbol-Letter-Number Pattern
tricks.explanation: Patterns often appear in groups of three elements.

tricks.title: Operation Pattern Identification
tricks.explanation: Quickly check number patterns like +, −, ×, or ÷.

tricks.title: Middle Element Check
tricks.explanation: In long series, first check around the middle positions.
tricks.example: If there are 20 elements, the 10th and 11th are the middle.

tricks.title: Stepwise Counting
tricks.explanation: Move step by step while counting positions.
tricks.example: 5th from the left, then 3rd from the right.
